Incorporating the January 2017 Beige Book, the tone remains cautiously constructive and broadly consistent with the FOMC’s “moderate” growth characterization, with a slight positive nudge versus the SLOOS-only read:
- Economic activity: Most districts reported modest-to-moderate expansion; manufacturing firmed and the energy sector stabilized—supportive of the baseline.
- Labor markets: Tight in many districts with modest-to-moderate wage gains, aligning with continued strengthening.
- Prices: Inflation pressures were modest and still below 2 percent on balance, consistent with low market-based inflation compensation.
- Credit conditions: Bank lending generally increased with largely unchanged standards, though CRE showed pockets of tightening—this partially offsets SLOOS’s tighter CRE/auto signals and foreign-bank caution.
- Sentiment: Business and consumer sentiment improved post-election, reinforcing a constructive backdrop.

Net: Beige Book corroborates moderate growth and labor-market strength and slightly tempers the SLOOS-driven caution on credit. I keep a cautiously constructive stance but edge the tone a bit higher.
